title: How the natural's elements, taken into the body, are stripped of their defiled garments and brought to rest
reading:
The four elemental faculties of the natural mind have been with the soul from the beginning; they are present in those who are holy, in those who are alive, and in the luminous states of the rational. Yet the brethren who learned what happened in the soul's first contest understood this: falsity from evil went inward together with these faculties, and the darkness of the proprium had mingled itself with them.

When these faculties come inward into the body — that is, when the rational accommodates itself into its outermost form — they leave behind in the flesh the defiled garments they had been wearing. But the garments stripped off do not simply vanish. They reveal themselves, and as they come uncovered they become a danger to the body that has just received the cleansed faculty.

There is an order in this uncovering. Beneath the self-binding of the proprium lies wrath; beneath the wrath, the very flow by which one self-loving state strips itself bare to give way to the next, in which the soul's deliberations strip themselves out of themselves: this is desire. Beneath the desire is bitterness, the falsity that should have nourished now afflicting; beneath the bitterness, hatred. When the light then strips these from the soul, what stands beneath is the flesh itself; and beneath the flesh, gloom, the falsity that obscures perception; and beneath the gloom, severity, the rational's hardness against itself. The strippings that perception itself performs lay bare the winds of shame, the disordered movements of thought when self-love sees its own nakedness. Beneath those, further still, lies the seat of the eightfold ways of corruption; and at the floor of the whole sequence stands the full twelvefold uncovering by which the natural mind is laid open.

This is the work the four elemental faculties perform, gathered inward in the proper ordering of the soul's nourishment. When they come into a body, they are refined, purified, and made to stand fast in the living likeness which is the New Man. There they are made alive; they receive into themselves the Lord's ordering of the rational; they are purified within that likeness; they come forth chosen and holy; and they reach their first rest, ascending to the inmost country where what is alive in the Lord dwells.

But where these same faculties enter a soul that goes on claiming what flows through it, they do not lay off their defilements. They multiply within it, and the soul sins through the very faculties that were given for its life. Such a state does not come to rest. Its end is the transfer of its condition into another substrate, under the Lord's discriminating judgment, until at last the recognition can be made.
